questions.q: In a workflow automation, what is a trigger?
options: The event that starts the workflow
The last step, which sends a notification
A person who approves each run
The app where your data is stored
questions.why: A trigger is the event that starts a workflow, such as a form submission, a new email, or a scheduled time. Everything after it is an action.

questions.q: Which task is usually the best first automation for a small business?
options: Rebuilding the whole website
A frequent, rule-based task close to revenue, like replying to new leads
An AI agent that handles every customer conversation
A report you run once a year
questions.why: High-volume, rule-based work close to revenue pays back fastest and carries little risk. Big, rare, or open-ended projects come later.

options: A paid plugin for a website
A message one app sends to another the moment something happens
A type of spam filter
A scheduled backup of your data
questions.why: A webhook is an automatic message an app sends to a web address when an event occurs, so other systems can react instantly instead of checking for changes over and over.

options: Rapid process analysis
Robotic process automation
Remote program access
Rules, prompts, and actions
questions.why: Robotic process automation uses software bots that mimic a person clicking and typing in an app's screens. It is most useful when a system has no API or integration.

questions.q: What is the main difference between rule-based automation and AI?
options: Automation is always more expensive
Automation follows rules you define, while AI handles language and judgment where rules fall short
AI cannot be used inside an automation
There is no real difference
questions.why: Rule-based automation does the same thing every time. AI interprets messy input such as emails and documents. The most reliable systems use AI steps inside rule-based workflows.

questions.q: An AI model gives a confident answer that sounds right but is wrong. What is this usually called?
options: A hallucination
A webhook
A timeout
A trigger
questions.why: Language models can produce fluent but incorrect output, often called a hallucination. Grounding the model in your own information and adding human review reduces the risk.

questions.q: What does "human in the loop" mean?
options: A person reviews or approves certain steps before the automation continues
A person does every step by hand
The automation emails the team a daily summary
Customers can opt out of automated messages
questions.why: Human in the loop means the workflow pauses for a person to check or approve a step, such as an AI-drafted reply or a large refund, before it goes ahead.

questions.q: Your automation should send a follow-up only if the lead has not replied yet. What do you need to add?
options: A second trigger
A condition, such as a filter or branch
A new CRM
An AI agent
questions.why: Conditions (filters, branches, or if/else paths) let a workflow check something, like whether a reply arrived, and choose what to do next.

questions.q: What is the best first step before automating a messy process?
options: Buy a new automation platform
Write the steps down and simplify the process
Add AI to absorb the mess
Automate it now and fix problems later
questions.why: Automating a messy process just makes the mess happen faster. Mapping and simplifying first makes the automation smaller, cheaper, and more reliable.
link: Lesson: mapping a process before you automate it

questions.q: How do you calculate an automation's payback period?
options: Build cost divided by the monthly net benefit
Monthly benefit multiplied by 12
Hours saved divided by team size
Running cost divided by build cost
questions.why: Payback period is the upfront cost divided by what the automation returns each month after its running costs. A $3,000 build that nets $1,000 a month pays back in three months.

explainer:
What the quiz covers

The questions span the core ideas behind business automation: how workflows start (triggers), how apps talk to each other (APIs and webhooks), the main kinds of automation (rule-based workflows, RPA, and AI), the risks of AI (hallucinations) and how to manage them (human review), and how to choose and justify a project (process mapping and payback).

Want to learn it properly?

Every question links to a lesson or guide. The free Automation 101 course teaches these concepts in eight short lessons, and the glossary defines every term in plain English.
faq: What are the basics of workflow automation?

A workflow starts with a trigger (an event such as a new form submission), then runs actions (create a contact, send a message, update a record), often with conditions that decide which actions run. Integrations and APIs let the workflow move data between apps.
Is this quiz scored or saved?
Your score is calculated in your browser and is not saved or sent anywhere. You can retake it as often as you like.
Where can I learn business automation for free?
Start with our free Automation 101 course, then read the guides in the resource center. Most automation platforms also publish free tutorials for their own tools.
